text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS
-- "Lionel Jospin postpones big choices until the autumn".
-- LVMH luxury goods group brings its stake in GrandMet to 6.29 percent, in bid to block its planned merger with Guinness .
-- Newspaper Le Monde considers buying weekly L'Express.
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux shareholders approve merger with Suez , new group will have a 210 billion francs turnover.
LA TRIBUNE
-- "Jospin commits himself to employment, not public deficits", proposes a pact on development and solidarity, announces a four percent hike in minimum wage SMIC.
-- Paris bourse greets Jospin's speech with mixed feelings.
-- Workers at insurer Axa UAP worried by consequences of the merger between the two companies.
-- Airbus [ARBU.CN] consortium wins order for 50 A319 and 100 options from Northwest Airlines .

-- Goodyear chairman Sam Gibara in an interview says he sees opportunities for growth in emerging markets notably in western Europe, expects an "important investment" in Europe, and is looking at France and other countries.
L'AGEFI

-- Jospin delivered a speech "dominated by tactical preoccupations, by joining parliamentary finance committees to ministers' work, Jospin seeks to commit the majority to the difficult task of preparing the budget".
-- Airbus Industrie about to securitise some 1.5 billion dollars worth of commercial loans.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Jospin's speech seen as "a bill and little income". The Prime Minister did not forget his campaign pledges, but remianed vague on how he would implement them and above all finance them, the paper adds.
-- Catering group Sodexho Alliance posts a 269.39 million francs profit for the first half.

-- Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet presented president Jacques Chirac with the bank's annual report yesterday, which will be made public Tuesday. Presidential spokeswoman said it showed a gradual cut in public deficits had increased trust in the franc and allowed for an historical decrease of interest rates.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- "Jospin unveils his Republican Pact", vows to respect campaign pledges, insists on ethics rather than costly social measures, the paper adds.
-- The merger of Lyonnaise des Eaux and Suez was approved yesterday.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- "Jospin puts job measures on hold", tells parliament of need to review France's finances.
